enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule for sections 13–19A: Sections 13–18 define consent, free consent, coercion, undue influence, fraud and misrepresentation; sections 19 and 19A prescribe when contracts affected by specified vitiating factors are voidable and the court’s power to set aside undue-influence contracts.

Definition: This group identifies when apparent agreement is legally impaired because consent was obtained through a statutorily recognised vitiating factor.

Ingredients / conditions:
1. Establish the parties’ agreement.
2. Identify the specific vitiating factor.
3. Prove its statutory ingredients and causal relevance to consent.
4. Apply the appropriate avoidance or court-set-aside remedy under sections 19 or 19A.
examples: A, a money-lender, advances ₹100 to B and by undue influence induces B to execute a bond for ₹200 with very high interest; the statutory illustration permits the court to set the bond aside on just terms.
problemApplication: Apply sections 13–19A: identify the precise statutory trigger, test each ingredient against the facts, consider the relevant exception or limitation, and state the statutory consequence.
keyTakeaways: Sections 13–18 define consent, free consent, coercion, undue influence, fraud and misrepresentation; sections 19 and 19A prescribe when contracts affected by specified vitiating factors are voidable and the court’s power to set aside undue-influence contracts.
This group identifies when apparent agreement is legally impaired because consent was obtained through a statutorily recognised vitiating factor.
